en: The Questions of King Milinda,
Great Chapter 9:
The Question on the Characteristic of Virtue (Sīla)
The King said:
"Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you said—that it is 'by other wholesome states'—what are those wholesome states?
"Virtue, Great King, faith, energy, mindfulness, and concentration—these are those wholesome states."
“What, venerable sir, is the characteristic of virtue?

“Virtue, great king, has the characteristic of being a foundation for all wholesome states. Virtue is the foundation for the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, the path-factors, the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the jhānas, the liberations, concentration, and the attainments.
Established in virtue, great king, the practitioner of yoga, relying on virtue and grounded in virtue...”
“One who develops the five faculties— the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom—
does not fall away from any wholesome states.
“Give me a simile,” he said.
“Just as, great king, whatever seeds and plants attain growth, increase, and abundance, they all do so by depending on the earth and being established upon the earth;

even so, great king, a practitioner of yoga, depending on virtue and being established in virtue, develops the five faculties: the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom.
“Give me a further simile,” [the king said].
“Just as, great king, whatever tasks requiring strength are performed, they are all performed depending on the earth and established upon the earth;

even so, great king, a practitioner of yoga, depending on virtue and established in virtue, develops the five faculties: the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom.
“Give me a further simile,” [the king said].
“Just as, great king, a city-builder, desiring to construct a city, first has the site for the city cleared,
has stumps and thorns pulled out, and has the ground leveled; thereafter, he divides it by demarcating streets, crossroads, junctions, and so forth, and thus constructs the city.”

“In the same way, great king, the practitioner of yoga, relying on virtue and established in virtue, develops the five faculties: the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom.
“Give me a further simile.
“Just as, great king, an acrobat wishing to display his skill digs the ground, has gravel and pebbles removed, and levels the earth; he then displays his skill upon that soft ground.”

In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga, relying upon virtue and established in virtue, develops the five faculties: the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom.
This was said, Great King, by the Blessed One:
“A wise man, established in virtue...”
Cultivating the mind and wisdom,
the ardent and discerning bhikkhu shall unravel this tangle.
This is the foundation for living beings like the earth,
and this is the root for the increase of wholesome qualities;
this is the gateway to the teaching of all the Victors.
“That which is the aggregate of virtue, possessing the excellent Pātimokkha.
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena!
This is the ninth question, on the characteristic of virtue.
